facts.setting: after a notice of noncompliance under 42 CFR 435.558(a)(1)
facts.value: a period of 30 calendar days beginning on the date on which such notice of noncompliance is received by the individual
facts.counts_from: the date on which the notice of noncompliance is received by the individual, presumed under 42 CFR 435.558(c)(4) to be 5 days after the date on the notice unless the individual shows that they did not receive it within the 5-day period
facts.note: The correction's only date of its own is its filing line, docs/domain/sources/federal-register/C1-2026-11094.xml:201 "Filed 6-26-26", so its source_date is 2026-06-26; it was published 2026-06-29. Whether the date of receipt is the first of the 30 calendar days is an open question. facts.value: Is considered to be received 5 days after the date on the notice, unless the applicant or beneficiary shows that he or she did not receive the notice within the 5-day period.
facts.note: The paragraph does not say whether the 5 days are calendar days; that is an open question. Dates of the sources as for notice-response-period. Whether a person showed they did not receive the notice within the 5-day period is the agency's determination.

facts.value: The State or local agency must send a notice at least 10 days before the date of action, except as permitted under §§ 431.213 and 431.214
facts.counts_from: the date of action, counted backward
facts.note: The exceptions are 42 CFR 431.213 and 431.214. Of those, only 431.213(d) is stored, in the June 3 printing, and it was not read for this fact; 431.214, and 431.201, which defines the date of action, are not stored. The section does not say whether the 10 days are calendar days; that is an open question. The eCFR XML prints no date of its own; the eCFR date is in the citation. Whether an exception applies to a person is the agency's determination.

facts.setting: on appeal, asking for a fair hearing
facts.value: not to exceed 90 days from the date that notice of action is mailed
facts.counts_from: the date that notice of action is mailed
facts.note: A ceiling, not a default: the agency must allow a reasonable time, and the State sets its length within the 90 days, as the row's State election says. The paragraph does not define a reasonable time or say whether the 90 days are calendar days; that is an open question. The 90 days count from mailing, where notice-response-period's 30 days count from receipt. The source line ends "to request a hearings." with that typo. The eCFR XML prints no date of its own; the eCFR date is in the citation. Whether a person asked in time is the agency's determination.
